reads: One local query hook replaces repeated fetch/loading/error and request ownership logic in SkillCenter.
Marketplace, installed skills, categories, key status, reviewed capabilities, profiles, interactions, npm and GitHub retain separate query state.
Same-tick refresh bursts collapse before network dispatch; later mutations cancel and replace older reads.
Late success, failure and JSON completion cannot overwrite a newer key or request, including after permission revocation and unmount.
Language changes only reload localized catalog/category data; profile and installed queries remain stable.
Stable refresh callbacks read the active key, so an older completed mutation refreshes the current locale; callbacks after unmount do not start reads.
Malformed catalog payloads become a visible retryable error instead of entering list state.
search: Keep 400ms debounce and six results per source; npm/GitHub resolve independently with visible partial failures.
Query changes and short/empty input hide prior results and errors immediately; removed the exit wrapper retaining obsolete search rows.
mutations: Reuse existing apiJson for standard read/write response validation; preserve explicit repair reason handling.
Manual, mutation and socket refresh paths share refreshSkills; header and retry share refreshAll.
Removed client install/uninstall/repair broadcasts already emitted by the server; retained generated-skill broadcast because that route does not emit it.
Keep installed cards visible while a background refresh is pending; rejected writes do not advance local success.

intermediateCorrections: Strict type check found two old setLoadError calls in refresh buttons; both now use refreshAll and the button is exercised in the event-coalescing test.
The installed-tab mutation test now waits for the existing page exit transition before asserting exactly one skill heading; assertions and timeouts were not weakened.
Follow-up review added unmount liveness, catalog-shape validation and current-key refresh callbacks; the earlier passing full run was superseded and final verification rerun.
limitations: Mounted component tests use simulated API responses; no live server or native client acceptance was performed.
AbortSignal is passed to direct API reads. Existing key-status/capability service helpers ignore cancellation, but their late results are discarded.
Requests from separate later events may still start again; the reduction in duplicate requests is limited to same-tick bursts, not an arbitrary debounce of mutations.
